citations.label: Beyond pass@1: A Reliability Science Framework for Long-Horizon LLM Agents (arXiv:2603.29231)
citations.excerpt: We show these properties diverge systematically as task duration grows, and that pass@1 on short tasks is structurally blind to this divergence.

citations.label: Can LLM Agents Be CFOs? Benchmarking Long-Horizon Resource Allocation in an Uncertain Enterprise Environment (arXiv:2603.23638)
citations.excerpt: Experiments across 23 LLMs and four agent frameworks show that current agents remain far from robust: only 15.4% of trials survive the full horizon, larger models do not reliably outperform smaller ones, and failures cascade across observation, action timing, and capital sizing.

citations.label: The Long-Horizon Task Mirage? Diagnosing Where and Why Agentic Systems Break (arXiv:2604.11978)
citations.excerpt: collecting 3100+ trajectories across four representative agentic domains to study horizon-dependent degradation patterns

citations.label: Measuring AI Ability to Complete Long Tasks (METR)
citations.excerpt: The length of tasks (measured by how long they take human professionals) that generalist frontier model agents can complete autonomously with 50% reliability has been doubling approximately every 7 months for the last 6 years.
